context.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening engine that evaluates payment authorizations and provides case management for fraud analysts. Its core purpose is to prevent fraudulent transactions while maintaining strict latency and compliance standards.

## Key Elements
- Payment Processor Systems / Acquirer
- Fraud Analysts and Risk Managers
- Fraud Screening Engine (AWS-hosted distributed service)
- AWS KMS, CloudTrail, and AWS Secrets Manager
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock

## Relationships
- Payment Processor Systems to Fraud Screening Engine via gRPC over mTLS (R-01, R-04)
- Fraud Analysts and Risk Managers to Fraud Screening Engine via HTTPS over TLS 1.3 (R-02, R-03)
- Fraud Screening Engine to AWS KMS via AWS SDK for data encryption (R-05)
- Fraud Screening Engine to Amazon S3 via AWS SDK for audit log storage (R-06)

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS (Fargate): Chosen for immutable infrastructure and zero-downtime model updates.
- gRPC over mTLS: Selected to meet sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Used for cost-effective, 7-year tamper-evident audit storage.
- AWS KMS: Implemented for envelope encryption and data-at-rest protection.

## Rationale
This architecture utilizes fully-managed AWS services to operate efficiently within a three-engineer team constraint and a strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It meets PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and low-latency performance requirements through optimized protocols and robust cloud security controls.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening engine processing card-not-present transactions for a mid-size payment processor. It provides sub-50ms fraud scoring and case management review capabilities.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers (Users)
* Amazon API Gateway (Ingress & WAF)
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go microservice on AWS ECS EC2)
* Case Management System (React SPA on S3 + CloudFront, Node.js/Express API on ECS)
* Compliance Reporting Worker (AWS Lambda)
* Data & Storage: Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon S3 with Object Lock
* Messaging & Fallback: Amazon SQS / Amazon Kinesis, API Gateway Circuit Breakers
* Security & Observability: AWS KMS (CMK), AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch

## Relationships
* Users to Amazon API Gateway: HTTPS / TLS 1.3
* API Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Engine: Internal gRPC over mTLS
* Scoring Engine to Amazon DynamoDB: AWS SDK over TLS 1.3
* Scoring Engine to Amazon SQS / Kinesis: Asynchronous event publishing over TLS 1.3
* Compliance Reporting Worker to Amazon S3 Object Lock: HTTPS via AWS SDK

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS on EC2: Provides predictable P99 latency (<50ms) and cost control within budget.
* Go: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency microservice scoring.
* Amazon DynamoDB: Delivers sub-millisecond feature store and case data lookups.
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year immutable audit retention.
* AWS Lambda: Eliminates operational overhead for scheduled compliance reporting.
* AWS KMS & Secrets Manager: Secures card data, audit logs, and runtime credentials.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless components and managed AWS services to minimize operational toil for a 3-engineer team while respecting a €25k monthly budget. Dedicated ECS EC2 instances and Go microservices guarantee sub-50ms performance and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

Amazon API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management for human analysts. It is operated by a three-engineer team on AWS under a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Amazon API Gateway HTTP API
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go microservice on AWS ECS EC2)
- Case Management System API (Node.js / Express on ECS)
- AWS WAFv2 WebACL
- Amazon CloudWatch
- AWS Secrets Manager

## Relationships
- Payment Processor -> Amazon API Gateway: Sends authorization requests [HTTPS / TLS 1.3 with mTLS]
- Fraud Analysts -> Amazon API Gateway: Accesses case management [HTTPS / JSON with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC JWT]
- Amazon API Gateway -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Proxies payment transactions [Internal gRPC over mTLS via AWS PrivateLink / VPC Link]
- Amazon API Gateway -> Case Management System API: Routes analyst requests [HTTPS / JSON]
- Amazon API Gateway -> Amazon CloudWatch: Streams structured JSON access logs [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs: Chosen for lower latency (<50ms P99) and 70% lower cost than REST APIs.
- AWS PrivateLink / VPC Link: Secures internal transit between API Gateway and ECS containers.
- AWS WAFv2: Provides edge rate-limiting and DDoS protection.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Secures JWT keys and mTLS trust store parameters.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless edge routing to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while meeting strict <50ms P99 latency and PCI-DSS compliance constraints. It maintains high availability and strict auditability within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
Real-time payment fraud screening engine for card-not-present transactions on AWS. Screens payment authorizations in under 50ms while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts and Risk Managers
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go microservice on AWS ECS EC2)
* API Handler Component, Feature Evaluator Component, Rules Engine Core, Audit Logger Component, Shadow Evaluator Component, and Model Registry Loader
* Amazon API Gateway, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon S3, Amazon SQS / Amazon Kinesis, AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, and Amazon CloudWatch

## Relationships
* Amazon API Gateway -> API Handler Component: Forwards payment transactions [Internal gRPC over mTLS]
* Feature Evaluator Component -> Amazon DynamoDB: Performs feature lookups [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]
* Audit Logger Component -> Amazon SQS / Kinesis: Publishes signed decision payloads [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]
* Model Registry Loader -> Amazon S3: Polls for Wasm models [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]
* Real-Time Scoring Engine -> AWS KMS & Secrets Manager: Requests keys and credentials [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]
* Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon CloudWatch: Sends metrics and logs [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
* Go (Gin/Goroutines): Chosen for high concurrency and low memory overhead to meet sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS.
* WebAssembly (Wasm): Enables secure sandboxing and hot-reloading of scoring models without downtime.
* Amazon DynamoDB: Provides single-digit millisecond feature lookups within budget constraints.
* AWS KMS: Ensures strict encryption, key rotation, and HMAC-SHA256 tamper-evident signing for audit compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages asynchronous Go goroutines and zero-copy in-memory communication to achieve sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS. AWS managed services and secure Wasm sandboxing satisfy PCI-DSS compliance, 7-year auditability, and zero-downtime updates within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget for a 3-engineer team.

Case Management System Frontend.analysis:
## Overview
- Provides a React-based single-page application hosted on Amazon S3 and delivered via Amazon CloudFront for fraud analysts and risk managers.
- Enables case management, transaction reviews, and zero-downtime rule updates while strictly enforcing data masking for PCI-DSS compliance.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts and Risk Managers (Users)
- Case Management System Frontend (React SPA on AWS S3 + CloudFront)
- Case Queue Component (React Component)
- Transaction Details Component (React Component)
- Rule Management Component (React Component)
- Audit Log Viewer Component (React Component)
- Amazon API Gateway / Case Management System API (Backend Services)
- AWS WAF (Security)

## Relationships
- Users access the frontend over HTTPS via Amazon CloudFront.
- Frontend communicates with backend services using HTTPS / JSON REST API with short-polling via React Query.
- AWS WAF inspects inbound requests at CloudFront to protect against attacks.

## Technology Stack
- React SPA: UI framework for a responsive single-page application experience.
- React Query: Manages state and short-polling data fetching.
- Amazon S3 & CloudFront: Static asset hosting and content delivery within budget constraints.
- AWS WAF: Edge security to mitigate DDoS and XSS risks.
- HttpOnly Cookies: Secure session token storage.

## Rationale
- Stateless short-polling and server-less static hosting minimize infrastructure complexity for a three-engineer team.
- Strict client-side masking and HttpOnly token management ensure PCI-DSS compliance and robust security.

Case Management System API.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management System API provides backend services for fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions and execute overrides. It ensures strict PCI-DSS compliance and maintainable operations for a 3-engineer team within budget.

## Key Elements
* **Case Controller / Router**: Express-based routing layer handling HTTP requests and JWT authentication.
* **Masking & Security Interceptor**: Middleware layer stripping PANs and validating RBAC scopes.
* **Case Service**: Core domain logic managing case states, analyst assignments, and aggregated DTO payloads.
* **Audit & Compliance Logger**: Component dispatching batched audit payloads asynchronously.
* **Data Access Layer**: Interfacing with Amazon DynamoDB for persistence.

## Relationships
* **Case Controller** invokes **Case Service** via internal TypeScript interfaces.
* **Audit & Compliance Logger** dispatches payloads to **Amazon SQS** asynchronously using AWS SDK.
* **Data Access Layer** reads and writes encrypted data to **Amazon DynamoDB** using AWS KMS.

## Technology Stack
* **Node.js / Express on AWS ECS Fargate**: Selected for zero-patching operational overhead and containerized deployment.
* **Amazon DynamoDB**: Chosen for low-latency scalable persistence of case data.
* **Amazon SQS with KMS**: Used to decouple audit logging and guarantee tamper-evident S3 delivery.
* **AWS KMS**: Utilized for envelope encryption of persistent case data and SQS message encryption.

## Rationale
This architecture fits requirements by utilizing serverless containers (ECS Fargate) and managed AWS services to minimize operational toil for a 3-engineer team. It enforces robust security boundaries and async SQS buffering to maintain compliance and performance without exceeding budget.

Compliance Reporting Worker.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for mid-size payment processors before approval, while providing a case management system for fraud analysts. The system ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability on AWS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts and Risk Managers
- Compliance Officers and Auditors
- Amazon API Gateway
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go microservice on AWS ECS EC2)
- Case Management System Frontend (React SPA on Amazon S3 + Amazon CloudFront)
- Case Management System API (Node.js / Express API on AWS ECS)
- Compliance Reporting Worker (AWS Lambda in Python)
- Amazon DynamoDB
- Amazon SQS / Amazon Kinesis
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- AWS KMS
- Amazon CloudWatch

## Relationships
- Case Management System Frontend -> Amazon API Gateway: HTTPS / REST API
- Amazon API Gateway -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Internal VPC routing
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB: Persists authorization inputs and decision logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Compliance Reporting Worker -> Amazon S3: Reads daily Parquet audit files [AWS SDK / S3 GetObject]
- Compliance Reporting Worker -> AWS KMS: Generates asymmetric cryptographic signatures (`ECC_NIST_P256`) [AWS KMS Sign API]
- Compliance Reporting Worker -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Stores signed daily compliance digests with 7-year retention tags [HTTPS / PutObject]
- Compliance Reporting Worker -> Amazon CloudWatch: Emits operational metrics and logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Lambda (Python 3.11): Serverless execution for cost-effective batch compliance reporting under budget constraints.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Implements tamper-evident, unalterable 7-year storage for regulatory audit logs.
- AWS KMS: Provides asymmetric cryptography (`ECC_NIST_P256`) for cryptographically signing compliance digests securely.
- Amazon DynamoDB & Kinesis Firehose: Streams and persists high-throughput payment decision logs into flat Parquet files.
- Terraform / AWS CDK: Infrastructure-as-Code for reproducible deployments and prevention of configuration drift.

## Rationale
The serverless, event-driven AWS architecture keeps operational overhead minimal for a three-engineer team while easily scaling to handle high-volume transaction logging. Strict IAM boundaries, KMS asymmetric signing, and S3 Object Lock natively satisfy the stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year tamper-evident auditability requirements within the fixed financial budget.

Amazon DynamoDB.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time fraud screening for payment authorizations and case management for fraud analysts. It ensures sub-50ms decision latency, strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a fixed budget.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go microservice on AWS ECS EC2)
- Case Management System API (Node.js / Express API on ECS)
- Hot Feature Table (DynamoDB Table, NoSQL)
- Case Management Table (DynamoDB Table, NoSQL)
- Compliance Reporting Worker (AWS Lambda)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Hot Feature Table: Queries feature attributes [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3, IAM Auth via VPC Gateway Endpoints]
- Case Management System API -> Case Management Table: Reads and updates case states [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3, HTTPS]
- DynamoDB Streams -> Compliance Reporting Worker: Triggers archival of closed cases [AWS Lambda]
- Compliance Reporting Worker -> Amazon S3: Stores historical audit logs [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- AWS DynamoDB: Provides single-digit millisecond latency for hot features and active cases while adhering to budget constraints.
- AWS KMS: Encrypts data at rest using customer-managed keys (CMK) with annual rotation for PCI-DSS compliance.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Archives historical audit logs to ensure 7-year tamper-evident retention cost-effectively.
- AWS VPC Gateway Endpoints: Secures data in transit by routing database traffic off the public internet.

## Rationale
This architecture balances ultra-low latency requirements with strict security and auditability mandates. Operational simplicity is maintained for a three-engineer team by leveraging serverless and managed AWS services within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Amazon SQS / Kinesis.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for mid-size payment processors to prevent fraud and enable suspicious payment reviews. It ensures strict sub-50ms latency, compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1, and tamper-evident 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go microservice on AWS ECS EC2)
- Case Management System Frontend (React SPA on S3 + CloudFront)
- Case Management System API (Node.js / Express API on ECS)
- Compliance Reporting Worker (AWS Lambda)
- Amazon SQS (Standard, FIFO, and Dead-Letter Queues)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- Amazon DynamoDB
- Amazon API Gateway
- Amazon CloudWatch
- AWS KMS
- Payment Processor Systems / Acquirer (External)

## Relationships
- Payment Processor -> Amazon API Gateway: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Amazon API Gateway -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Routes scoring requests [HTTP/JSON over VPC internal network]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS: Publishes asynchronous case and audit events [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]
- Amazon SQS (Audit Queue) -> Compliance Reporting Worker: Invokes processing [AWS Lambda event source mapping]
- Compliance Reporting Worker -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Persists immutable audit records [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management System Frontend: Reviews flagged cases [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Case Management System API -> Amazon DynamoDB: Reads/writes case data [AWS SDK over TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- **Compute:** AWS ECS (EC2 launch type) for low-latency microservices; AWS Lambda for serverless compliance reporting workers.
- **Frontend Storage & Delivery:** Amazon S3 combined with Amazon CloudFront for static asset hosting.
- **Database:** Amazon DynamoDB for low-latency case management storage.
- **Messaging & Buffering:** Amazon SQS (Standard, FIFO, and Dead-Letter Queues) for asynchronous event handling and fail-open resilience.
- **Audit Storage:** Amazon S3 with Object Lock for tamper-evident 7-year record retention.
- **Security & Encryption:** AWS KMS with Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) and TLS 1.3 enforcing data encryption at rest and in transit.
- **Monitoring:** Amazon CloudWatch for metrics, operational alarms, and logging.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational toil for a lean three-engineer team while easily respecting the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Standardizing entirely on SQS instead of Kinesis ensures predictable scaling, strict audit sequencing via FIFO queues, and robust fail-open continuity under 1 minute.

Amazon CloudWatch.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening protects card-not-present authorizations from fraud for a mid-size payment processor. It provides sub-50ms scoring decisions, manual case management, and strict PCI-DSS compliance within a fixed AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go microservice on AWS ECS EC2)
- Case Management System API (Node.js / Express API on ECS)
- Case Management System Frontend (React SPA on S3 + CloudFront)
- Amazon API Gateway
- Amazon DynamoDB
- Amazon SQS / Amazon Kinesis
- Compliance Reporting Worker (AWS Lambda)
- Amazon CloudWatch (Log Groups, Metric Filters, Alarms, Logs Insights, Synthetics)
- AWS KMS and Amazon S3 with Object Lock

## Relationships
- Amazon API Gateway -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Forwards payment authorization requests [HTTPS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB: Persists transaction state and audit records [AWS SDK over TLS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS / Amazon Kinesis: Queues asynchronous review and audit events [AWS SDK over TLS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine / Case Management API -> Amazon CloudWatch: Emits EMF metrics and redacted logs [AWS SDK over HTTPS]
- CloudWatch Alarm Evaluator -> Amazon SNS: Dispatches operational and business alerts [HTTPS]
- Amazon Kinesis Firehose -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Streams logs for 7-year immutable retention [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud provider ensuring managed scalability and compliance features
- Go: Chosen for the scoring engine to meet sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS
- React SPA & Node.js/Express: Powers the case management UI and API
- Amazon DynamoDB: Provides low-latency NoSQL data persistence
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Enforces tamper-evident 7-year audit retention (R-06)
- Amazon CloudWatch & AWS KMS: Handles observability, EMF metrics, and encrypted log storage under strict IAM controls

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to handle 3,000 TPS under a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It strictly separates hot operational observability from 7-year immutable storage in S3, ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and auditability.
